lions of al rassan.title: The lions of Al-Rassan
lions of al rassan.author: Guy Gavriel Kay
lions of al rassan.why: A medieval-Spain-inspired world of three peoples, a tale of war, friendship and honour that readers call magnificent.

blacktongue thief.title: The Blacktongue Thief
blacktongue thief.author: Christopher Buehlman
blacktongue thief.why: A thief and a knight travel a grim world with sharp humour and gore; the author-read audiobook has readers laughing aloud.

mountain in the sea.title: Mountain in the Sea
mountain in the sea.author: Ray Nayler
mountain in the sea.why: A near-future story of contact with an intelligent octopus, a hacker and ethics; full of ideas that stay with readers.

sky daddy.title: Sky Daddy
sky daddy.author: Kate Folk
sky daddy.why: A strange, funny novel about a woman who falls for aircraft; absurd but sharp about modern dating.

one.title: The One
one.author: John Marrs
one.why: A near-future thriller where a DNA test matches you to your soulmate; readers were hooked from page one.

killer angels.title: The Killer Angels
killer angels.author: Michael Shaara
killer angels.why: The Battle of Gettysburg through the eyes of its generals, a Pulitzer-winning war novel that works even for readers who avoid war fiction.

beautyland.title: Beautyland
beautyland.author: Marie-Helene Bertino
beautyland.why: A strange, tender novel about a girl who believes she is an alien; sublime despite its odd premise.

lamb the gospel according to biff christ.title: Lamb: The Gospel According to Biff, Christ's Childhood Pal
lamb the gospel according to biff christ.author: Christopher Moore
lamb the gospel according to biff christ.why: The missing years of Jesus told by his best friend, with irreverent humour; readers say it hooks from the start.

angle of repose.title: Angle of repose
angle of repose.author: Wallace Stegner
angle of repose.why: A retired historian pieces together his grandparents' pioneering life in the American West; slow, rich and rewarding.

castle.title: The Castle
castle.author: Franz Kafka
castle.why: A surveyor tries to reach a castle's authorities in endless red tape; odd, funny and full of dread.

burial rites.title: Burial Rites
burial rites.author: Hannah Kent
burial rites.why: A woman awaits execution in 19th-century Iceland, told in beautiful prose; readers recommend anything by Kent.

prophet.title: The Prophet
prophet.author: Kahlil Gibran
prophet.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

trees.title: The Trees
trees.author: Percival L. Everett
trees.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

parable of the talents.title: Parable of the Talents
parable of the talents.author: Octavia E. Butler
parable of the talents.why: Butler's grim sequel about a religious fascist America and a prophet's family; not enjoyable but powerful and chillingly relevant.

exquisite corpse.title: Exquisite Corpse
exquisite corpse.author: Poppy Z. Brite
exquisite corpse.why: A serial killer story that is lyrical and gruesome; a one-sitting read that stays in the mind.

open throat.title: Open Throat
open throat.author: Henry Hoke
open throat.why: A mountain lion narrates a short, strange, poetic novel; readers say it is really good if you accept its vision.

little friend.title: The Little Friend
little friend.author: Donna Tartt
little friend.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

pushing ice.title: Pushing Ice
pushing ice.author: Alastair Reynolds
pushing ice.why: Humans pursue an alien object across deep space and time; the timescales stay in readers' minds for years.

luminaries.title: The Luminaries
luminaries.author: Eleanor Catton
luminaries.why: A gold-rush mystery structured by astrology in 1860s New Zealand; long, intricate and absorbing.

fear and loathing in las vegas.title: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas
fear and loathing in las vegas.author: Hunter S. Thompson
fear and loathing in las vegas.why: A drug-fuelled road trip through Nevada, wildly funny and famously chaotic; a cult classic.

island of the blue dolphins.title: Island of the Blue Dolphins
island of the blue dolphins.author: Scott O’Dell
island of the blue dolphins.why: A girl survives alone on an island for years; a short children's survival classic readers recommend.

killers of the flower moon.title: Killers of the Flower Moon
killers of the flower moon.author: David Grann
killers of the flower moon.why: The true crime story of the murders of Osage people for their oil wealth, told like a thriller.

deadly education.title: A Deadly Education
deadly education.author: Naomi Novik
deadly education.why: A cynical girl survives a deadly magical school; fast, sharp and ironic.

passenger.title: The Passenger
passenger.author: Cormac McCarthy
passenger.why: A salvage diver, a missing passenger and a haunted sister; a tough, odd novel for devoted McCarthy readers.

separate peace.title: A Separate Peace
separate peace.author: John Knowles
separate peace.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

horse.title: Horse
horse.author: Geraldine Brooks
horse.why: A racehorse's story links centuries of American history and art; remembered long after finishing.

gateway.title: Gateway
gateway.author: Frederik Pohl
gateway.why: A prospector gambles on alien-made ships and is haunted by guilt; a classic of classic space SF.

revival.title: Revival
revival.author: Stephen King
revival.why: A preacher, a fixation on electricity and the dark where it leads; its final pages impress its fans.

borne.title: Borne
borne.author: Jeff VanderMeer
borne.why: A scavenger finds a living creature in a ruined city ruled by a giant bear; weird, atmospheric and beloved.

all quiet on the western front.title: All Quiet on the Western Front
all quiet on the western front.author: Erich Maria Remarque
all quiet on the western front.why: A German soldier's view of the First World War; bleak, human and timeless anti-war writing.

unconsoled.title: The Unconsoled
unconsoled.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
unconsoled.why: A pianist arrives in a town where the logic is dream-like; slow, strange and demanding Ishiguro.

shades of grey.title: Shades of Grey
shades of grey.author: Jasper Fforde
shades of grey.why: A colour-ruled caste society in a strange future Britain; funny, inventive and clever.

bone clocks.title: The Bone Clocks
bone clocks.author: David Mitchell
bone clocks.why: A woman's life tangled with a secret war of immortals across decades; sprawling and ambitious.

deluge.title: The Deluge
deluge.author: Stephen Markley
deluge.why: A near-future climate collapse seen from many angles and characters; a heavy, long novel that readers call a favourite.

wind and truth.title: Wind and Truth
wind and truth.author: Brandon Sanderson
wind and truth.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

redwall.title: Redwall
redwall.author: Brian Jacques
redwall.why: Mice defend their abbey from a rat warlord in a classic animal adventure with feasts and bravery.

age of innocence.title: The Age of Innocence
age of innocence.author: Edith Wharton
age of innocence.why: A lawyer is torn between a proper fiancee and a forbidden love in Gilded Age New York.

land.title: Land
land.author: Maggie O'Farrell
land.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

anne of green gables.title: Anne of Green Gables
anne of green gables.author: Lucy Maud Montgomery
anne of green gables.why: An imaginative orphan finds a home on Prince Edward Island; a gentle, funny children's classic.

americanah.title: Americanah
americanah.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
americanah.why: A Nigerian woman's love story across Lagos, America and Britain; sharp on race and identity.

last samurai.title: The Last Samurai
last samurai.author: Helen Dewitt
last samurai.why: A single mother raises a genius son by teaching him languages; clever, odd and brilliant.

immense world.title: An Immense World
immense world.author: Ed Yong
immense world.why: A tour through how animals sense the world, with creatures' strange perception; readers say it breaks the human-centred view.

augustus.title: Augustus
augustus.author: John Williams
augustus.why: The life of the Roman emperor told in letters and documents; praised as Williams's best.

six of crows.title: Six of Crows
six of crows.author: Leigh Bardugo
six of crows.why: A crew of misfits plans an impossible heist in a fantasy city; described as Ocean's Eleven with magic.

madame bovary.title: Madame Bovary
madame bovary.author: Gustave Flaubert
madame bovary.why: A bored provincial wife's romantic delusions lead to ruin; the standard realist novel.

empire of the vampire.title: Empire of the Vampire
empire of the vampire.author: Jay Kristoff
empire of the vampire.why: A vampire-hunter tells his life to a historian in a grim world of monsters; a long book readers can't put down.

snow child.title: The Snow Child
snow child.author: Eowyn Ivey
snow child.why: Not a clear recommendation of this book.

zen and the art of motorcycle maintenanc.title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
zen and the art of motorcycle maintenanc.author: Robert M. Pirsig
zen and the art of motorcycle maintenanc.why: A motorcycle trip and an inquiry into quality; layered and philosophical, with many readers re-reading it.

world war z.title: World War Z
world war z.author: Max Brooks
world war z.why: A series of interviews tell the story of a zombie war; clever, global and shaped like an oral history.

heroes.title: The Heroes
heroes.author: Joe Abercrombie
heroes.why: One bloody battle fought in a few days, with grim comedy and well-drawn soldiers; fans love its brutality.

talisman.title: The talisman
talisman.author: Stephen King and Peter Straub
talisman.why: A boy crosses America and a parallel world to save his dying mother; a King and Straub team-up.

big swiss.title: Big Swiss
big swiss.author: Jen Beagin
big swiss.why: A phone-sex operator listens to a woman's therapy sessions; hilarious, wild and sexual.

train dreams.title: Train dreams
train dreams.author: Denis Johnson
train dreams.why: A railway worker's life in the early American West, short and lyrical; one reader found it underwhelming.

diamond age.title: The Diamond Age
diamond age.author: Neal Stephenson
diamond age.why: A girl gets an interactive book that shapes her life in a nano-tech future; clever world-building.

wide sargasso sea.title: Wide Sargasso Sea
wide sargasso sea.author: Jean Rhys
wide sargasso sea.why: The story of the mad woman in the attic from Jane Eyre, told from her side in the Caribbean.

eyes of the dragon.title: The Eyes of the Dragon
eyes of the dragon.author: Stephen King
eyes of the dragon.why: A prince is framed and the kingdom is in danger in a straightforward medieval fantasy from King.

redshirts.title: Redshirts
redshirts.author: John Scalzi
redshirts.why: Crew members on a starship notice their friends keep dying; fans of Star Trek enjoy this light, fast joke.

little women.title: Little Women
little women.author: Louisa May Alcott
little women.why: Four March sisters grow up during the Civil War; warm, much-loved and a good choice for readers young or old.

deep.title: The Deep
deep.author: Rivers Solomon
deep.why: Descendants of drowned African women live underwater and keep their people's memory; short, moving and haunting.

carrie.title: Carrie
carrie.author: Stephen King
carrie.why: A bullied teen with telekinesis takes revenge; King's short debut that hooked readers young.

north and south.title: North and South
north and south.author: Elizabeth Cleghorn Gaskell
north and south.why: A southern woman moves to a northern mill town and meets a proud manufacturer; romance and social class.

cannery row.title: Cannery Row
cannery row.author: John Steinbeck
cannery row.why: Life among the poor and cheerful residents of a California fishing street; short and warmly written.

light.title: Light
light.author: M. John Harrison
light.why: A strange and gorgeous space opera with drugs and dread, ranked among readers' top five.

quicksilver.title: Quicksilver
quicksilver.author: Callie Hart
quicksilver.why: A romantasy with a dangerous love story and fast plot; one reader calls it the best of five years.

i am legend.title: I Am Legend
i am legend.author: Richard Matheson
i am legend.why: The last man on Earth among vampires; the final chapter lingers in readers' minds for years.

christmas carol.title: A Christmas Carol
christmas carol.author: Charles Dickens
christmas carol.why: Scrooge is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve; a short, familiar ghost story that still works for most readers.

alienist.title: The Alienist
alienist.author: Caleb Carr
alienist.why: A psychologist helps hunt a killer in 1890s New York; far better than the TV series, fans say.

stormlight archive.title: The Stormlight Archive
stormlight archive.author: Brandon Sanderson
stormlight archive.why: A vast epic series about knights, spren and a world of storms, loved by readers for its worldbuilding.

gift of fear.title: The Gift of Fear
gift of fear.author: Gavin de Becker
gift of fear.why: A security expert explains how to read danger signs and trust your instincts; named required reading.

secret garden.title: The Secret Garden
secret garden.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
secret garden.why: A lonely orphan finds a hidden garden and heals; a gentle children's classic.
